name: Amminadab
overview: Amminadab was a male member of the tribe of Levi who held the position of chief over the sons of Uzziel. His leadership role is specifically noted in 1 Chronicles 15:10, highlighting his standing within the Levitical community. There are no additional notes recorded about him beyond this designation.
namesAndTitles: The name Amminadab means '[my] people are generous,' which reflects a meaningful Hebrew proper name, though it was not given by God. This name appears explicitly in 1 Chronicles 15:10 and conveys a positive attribute associated with his identity.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Amminadab as a descendant of Uzziel, establishing his lineage within the Levitical family. No other familial relationships are recorded beyond this connection in 1 Chronicles 15:10.
scriptureSignificance: Amminadab's significance in the biblical narrative centers on his leadership as chief over the sons of Uzziel, a notable division within the tribe of Levi. His role underscores the organized structure of Levitical families and their responsibilities in Israel's worship life. Though details are limited, his mention affirms the importance of faithful leadership within God's appointed priestly tribe.
